text:
lia chen: heads up — planning thread for Q3/Q4 capacity phasing. want to align procurement windows, region rollouts, and utilization targets before next exec sync.
kevin m.: sounds good. primary constraint is vendor lead times — 12–18 weeks for the A100 class and 20+ for next-gen. we need order cutoff dates by EOW.
marco gonzalez: also factoring EU customs delays and import paperwork. recommend a conservative 4-week buffer for eu shipments.
anita rao: can we sketch target utilization per fleet for launch? Dedicated customers expect 40–60% steady utilization to make pricing work.
samuel: from telemetry, hosted API spikes make average utilization unpredictable. suggestion: target baseline 35% overall, with autoscale headroom to 70% for bursts.
lia chen: proposal: two procurement windows (early Q3 and late Q4) with a 25% buffer capacity in each new region to cover onboarding + pilot customers. thoughts?
kevin m.: +1 but prefer phasing: initial minimum order smaller to validate performance and bin packing, then second wave larger to hit committed SLA capacity.
marco gonzalez: propose region sequence: na -> eu -> apac. apac pilots require local partners/marketplace listing for faster procurement in some clouds.
anita rao: we should lock a holdback for Dedicated customers — reserved pools that map to committed contracts. that affects usable fleet for hosted temporarily.
lia chen: agree. holdback ratio proposal: 20% of new capacity reserved for Dedicated or enterprise onboarding for first 90 days.
samuel: operational note: need cooldown policy to avoid immediate reorders from transient spikes. recommend 6-week cooldown after a procurement window before ordering more for the same SKU/region.
kevin m.: cooldown + telemetry gating: only trigger new orders if 3 metrics all cross thresholds for 10 days: (1) 90th pct latency degradation, (2) queue growth > 25% baseline, (3) utilization > 65% sustained.
marco gonzalez: ok — add checklist for customs/KYC validation before placing EU orders. can be a gating item in the procurement playbook.
lia chen: draft schedule (very rough):
```
window-1: order cutoff 2026-06-15 -> arrival 2026-09-01 -> na + eu pilot
window-2: order cutoff 2026-10-01 -> arrival 2027-01-10 -> eu scale + apac pilot
```
kevin m.: looks plausible. we need contingent plan if vendor delays push arrival >+30 days: shift traffic via smart routing and temporarily increase burst quota in public clouds.
anita rao: launch criteria for a region:
- baseline perf SLO met on pilot traffic
- Dedicated holdback allocated
- infra runbooks + oncall assigned
- billing and marketplace/legal cleared
if any fail, we delay rollout or keep region restricted to internal testing.
samuel: can we add a utilization OKR: "Fleet utilization efficiency — maintain >=35% avg across fleet while meeting 99th pct latency SLO"? measurable with current observability.
lia chen: yes. add secondary KR: "Procurement lead time variance <= 2 weeks" to push vendors on predictability.
marco gonzalez: risks: SKU obsolescence, customs, single-vendor dependency. mitigations: dual-sourcing for critical SKUs, staggered orders, and small initial buys.
lia chen: action items:
- kevin: produce vendor cutoff calendar + MOQ for top 3 SKUs by Tue
- marco: update customs/KYC checklist and estimated buffers by Wed
- anita: model holdback economics and pricing impact for Dedicated by Thu
- samuel: add telemetry gating rules to autoscale + procurement dashboard by Fri
ops-bot: reminder created: #procurement-planning meeting Monday 10:00am
lia chen: thanks all — we'll consolidate into the roadmap doc and circulate before the exec sync.
